newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no odd Moscow moves after Lebed firing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no odd Moscow moves after Lebed firing.

text.p: The White House said the U.S. embassy in Moscow had reported no unusual activity Thursday after Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked his national security chief Alexander Lebed.

"The embassy reports there is no unusual activity in Moscow in response to President Yeltsin's announcement that we're aware of," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters travelling with President Bill Clinton on a campaign trip.
McCurry said Russia's constitution allowed for such action and "he (Yeltsin) seems to have acted in ways consistent with those constitutional prerogatives."
He said Clinton had been briefed on the situation by national security aides.
